CVE-2026-109083.description:
Improper isolation or compartmentalization vulnerability in Apache Syncope.

CVE-2026-126682.title: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via exponent-notation string in INTEGER encoding
CVE-2026-126682.description:
Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via exponent-notation string in INTEGER encoding.

The encoder routes any value with abs >= 2**31 to i2osp without validating that it is an integer. A string in exponent notation such as "1e8000" passes that threshold. Math::BigInt expands it to an 8001-digit integer, and i2osp's per-octet conversion loop is quadratic in that size.

An attacker who controls encoded INTEGER values can exhaust CPU with a short exponent-notation string.

On the resume branch the code instead does boot_read_swap_size(fap, &bs->swap_size); copy_size = bs->swap_size; and passes the value to swap_run() with no re-derivation and no bound.

CVE-2026-62975.description: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to version 1.5.1, the RAMFS-backed FILE implementation accepts AtomicWriteFile(record-access) requests that replace existing records with caller-controlled content. If a client replaces a record with shorter data, the backend can shrink the heap allocation and then continue processing with a trailing-copy length derived from the old layout. During that replace path, the RAMFS backend computes the trailing-copy length from the old file layout, then shrinks the heap allocation, and finally uses the stale length in memmove(). CVE-2026-93658.title: uutils coreutils 0.0.18 before 0.10.0 Privilege Escalation via setuid
CVE-2026-93658.description: uutils coreutils versions before 0.10.0 apply setuid or setgid mode to install destinations before finalizing ownership changes, allowing privileged users to leave setuid executables owned by the privileged invoker when ownership changes fail. Attackers can execute leftover setuid files with elevated privileges when ownership change operations fail on capability-restricted systems.

CVE-2026-97870.title: Apache TomEE: Missing authentication for Hessian endpoints in embedded HTTP server
CVE-2026-97870.description: When Hessian remoting endpoints are served by the embedded HTTP server, configured authentication and transport security requirements are silently ignored. A remote unauthenticated attacker can invoke the exposed EJB methods without credentials or over an unencrypted connection. Only deployments that use the embedded HTTP server rather than Tomcat and rely on these settings are affected. Users are recommended to block network access to Hessian endpoints from untrusted clients, or to migrate to another remoting protocol.

CVE-2026-99483.title: ALSA: pcmtest: handle multiple wraps in random capture fill
CVE-2026-99483.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: pcmtest: handle multiple wraps in random capture fill

The random capture helpers assume that the data generated for one timer
tick wraps the DMA ring at most once. However, b_rw describes 200 ms of
audio because the timer runs at 5 Hz, so it can be several times larger
than a small ring.

For 48 kHz, S16_LE, four-channel capture with a 512-frame buffer, the DMA
ring is 4096 bytes while one tick generates 76800 bytes. After filling the
4096-byte tail, the existing code issues a second 72704-byte write from the
ring base, writing 68608 bytes beyond the ring. Both interleaved and
non-interleaved capture are affected.

KASAN reports the first write into the adjacent free page as a
use-after-free in the random-byte generator. The underlying defect is an
out-of-bounds write from the live DMA ring, not a stale DMA allocation.

Split each random write repeatedly at the interleaved ring or per-channel
block boundary.…

CVE-2026-99609.title: ALSA: usx2y: Require a buffer of two URBs
CVE-2026-99609.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: usx2y: Require a buffer of two URBs

usx2y_urb_capt_retire() wraps the ring buffer once per packet and
usx2y_urb_play_prepare() once per URB of nr_of_packs() packets of up to
50 frames. Both assume that the data fits in the buffer, and the hw
constraints only require about two 1 ms periods, so a packet larger
than the buffer on capture, or a URB larger than the buffer on playback,
violates that assumption.

Constrain SNDRV_PCM_HW_PARAM_BUFFER_SIZE in snd_usx2y_pcm_open() to at
least two URBs, 2 * nr_of_packs() * 50 frames, for both directions. The
bound is in frames and derived from the driver's own packet limit, so it
does not read the endpoint, whose altsetting is only selected in
prepare. Two URBs rather than one, because the position advances by a
URB on playback and only moves when a URB is less than the whole buffer.
